newsitem.title: ITALY: TIM to recapitalise foreign cellular arm.
newsitem.headline: TIM to recapitalise foreign cellular arm.

text.p: Telecom Italia Mobile (TIM) said on Wednesday that it would pump over one trillion lire into its international mobile phone division allowing it buy control of its parent's Greek mobile phone operation.
TIM will recapitalise Stet Mobile Holding and use the money to take a controlling stake in Greek cellular phone company Stet Hellas.
The 74.8 percent holding in Stet Hellas is now held by Stet International, a division of Telecom Italia.

TIM said in a statement that it would lead the recapitalisation of Stet Mobile Holding, putting an initial 951.2 billion lire into the group followed by a further 313 billion lire at a later, unspecified, stage.
Stet International's majority holding in Stet Hellas is valued at some 990 billion lire.
The operation will leave TIM's stake in Stet Mobile Holding unchanged at 49 percent stake. Stet International will hold 38.98 percent of the unit and Telecom Italia 12.02 percent.
In addition, TIM will gradually take over management of Stet Mobile Holding's international cellular operations in Brazil, France, Austria and the Czech Republic.
At the end of the recapitalisation, Stet Mobile will have net assets of some 2.7 trillion lire, the statement said.

The operation is part of a reorganisation within the Telecom Italia group, following the merger earlier this month of the phone operating company Telecom Italia and the telecom holding Stet. The whole group is due to privatised later this year.
